title: 2023-2024 Retail Sales Performance Report
executive_summary: Analysis of 520 cleaned retail orders reveals total revenue of $445,325.09 with a strong 10.1% year-over-year growth in 2024. The East region leads regional performance, while 2024 quarterly trends show revenue peaking in Q3. High-discount electronics orders represent a modest portion of sales, and revenue distribution is skewed by a significant gap between mean and median order values.

key_findings.statement: The business generated a total revenue of $445,325.09 across 520 orders, resulting in an average order value of $856.39.
Regional revenue performance was led by the East region ($130,516.69), followed by North ($124,845.75), West ($99,428.16), and South ($90,534.49).

In 2024, quarterly revenue showed an upward trend through the first three quarters, peaking in Q3 at $71,674.99 before slightly contracting to $68,948.71 in Q4. Q1 recorded the lowest revenue at $36,108.31.
Total revenue increased from $211,976.29 in 2023 to $233,348.80 in 2024, representing a year-over-year increase of 10.1%.
There were 22 orders in the Electronics category with a discount of 20% or higher, contributing $50,035.33 to total revenue.

Order revenue distribution is highly skewed: while the mean is $856.39, the median is only $313.28. The standard deviation is $1,295.74, with individual order values ranging from a minimum of $5.27 to a maximum of $7,844.02.
The customer base consists of 222 unique customers. The top customer generated $27,793.13 in revenue, accounting for 6.2% of total revenue.

limitations: The analysis relies on a single export file and may not reflect real-time transactional data.
Customer concentration analysis is limited to the top single customer; broader concentration metrics (e.g., top 5 or top 10) were not calculated.
No profitability analysis was performed; high-discount revenue figures do not account for margin impact.
conclusion: The business demonstrated solid growth in 2024, expanding revenue by over 10% year-over-year. While the East and North regions are the primary revenue drivers, the significant gap between mean and median order values suggests that a subset of high-value orders disproportionately influences average metrics. The customer base appears reasonably diversified, with no single customer exceeding a 7% revenue share.
